Dossier 1: Constitution anti-discrimination incl. gender identity, hate crime penalties for GI, same-sex legal, no criminalisation. No administrative LGR (resident gap — not traveler exposure). Socially: pride parades, legal aid org, but political hate speech, threats to pride, dated 2015 survey of LGBTQ (out of scope per rule 17 — dated and LGBTQ-wide). No documented traveler-facing restrictions. No trans-specific violence data. Inconsistent implementation. Subnational: capital organizing, threats but no incident. This is a jurisdiction with legal protections on paper, documented social friction/hostility in political sphere, no documented visitor-facing exposure. Score maybe 0.60-0.68. The dossier documents societal hostility elements (politicians' hate speech, death threats to artist, pride under threats) but tier 3 at most with some recourse (hate crime law, discrimination law, NGO legal aid). Rule of law inconsistent implementation. I'd say ~0.62.

Dossier 2: Never criminalised same-sex, no laws against GI. But documented police targeting of trans women (forced bathing, extortion), 135+ harassment cases, 38% of trans women surveyed arrested with 90% because of transness, violence against LGBTI listed as significant human rights issue, 100+ incidents. Prison transfer for post-surgery trans women to women's facility (positive-ish but surgery-gated). No legal recognition, no non-discrimination legislation. Official cooperation on paper (UPR acceptances, tourism ministry welcoming LGBT tourists, media ministry asking not to mock). Documented state-tolerated targeting: police practice targeting trans sex workers — tier 2. Street violence documented as pattern (135 cases, 100+ incidents). This is a case where society is somewhat tolerant/official posture positive but police conduct is bad — for sex workers mainly. Traveler risk: police extortion of trans people. Score maybe 0.42-0.50. The police practice is targeted at sex workers, not all trans visitors, but 38% arrest rate among trans women is high. Documented societal harassment on streets. I'd go ~0.45.

Dossier 3: Same-sex marriage, LGR without surgery, criminalisation of transphobia, X markers on passports/IDs, custody placement resolution with self-declaration and preference, bathroom rights affirmed, courts fine businesses. But: documented violence, drink-spiking robberies, prison census showing trans women in masculine units in one state (state practice contradicting national norm), minors' care ban (resident). Subnational: state prison system housing in male units — but that's residents in custody, not visitors... Actually detention is traveler-relevant if arrested. The national resolution is protective. Documented societal hostility exists but strong recourse (hate crime law functioning, court awards, femicide law extension). Worst feature tier 3 with strong recourse, plus one state's prison practice (tier 1-ish but only for incarcerated, and national rule exists yet practice diverges — institutional failure). Score ~0.68-0.75.

Dossier 4: New LGR act 2025 (resident). Hate crime/hate speech covering trans since 2018/2019. Changing-room restriction by a national swimming pool chain (Oct 2025) — universal-exposure-ish facility restriction for visitors at that chain. Care narrowed for minors (resident). Organized opposition, political violence against trans advocates, sex-based-rights platform. Hate speech law not applied to religious figures (acquittal through supreme court). International travel index rates highly LGBT-friendly. Score: facility restriction at one chain (limited), documented organized hostility but strong legal protections. ~0.70? The pool chain restriction is a documented traveler-facing exposure but limited to one chain. Also mentions legal gender recognition with medical conditions. I'd say 0.68-0.72.

Dossier 5: Self-ID law, X marker, hate crime, bathroom protected, marriage, conversion ban, ranked top, dedicated LGBT+ travel advice from foreign government, hate crime reporting with low counts (16, 11, 7). Very strong. Score ~0.88-0.92. Some noted gaps, hate crimes rising slightly but small counts. I'd go 0.90.

Now ordering: 5 highest (0.90), then 3 (0.72), 4 (0.70), 1 (0.62), 2 (0.45).

Dossier 3 vs 4: Dossier 3 has stronger protections (X markers on passports, custody preference protocol, court rulings, world's largest pride) but also documented violence patterns (drink-spiking robberies, fatal dating-app robberies, trans candidates facing threats) and one state's prison practice violating national norm. Dossier 4 has a facility restriction (pool chain changing rooms) — universal exposure at that chain, plus organized political opposition and violence against advocates. Hmm. Rule 14's precedence ladder: dossier 4's worst documented feature is a private company's changing room restriction (tier 1-ish but private, contested legally). Dossier 3's worst is prison placement divergence in one state (tier 1 for incarcerated) plus documented street violence at some scale. Dossier 3 also has strong protective machinery. I'd rate 3 slightly higher: 0.73 vs 0.68. Actually the pool restriction reaching "ordinary public facilities" is a universal-exposure measure but limited to one chain and legally contested. Dossier 3's national custody resolution is protective but practice diverges — institutional failure documented. Hmm, both have flaws. Let me set 3 = 0.72, 4 = 0.69.

Dossier 1: Let's reconsider. Legal protections (GI discrimination ground, hate crime penalties), but implementation inconsistent, political hate speech common, pride under threats, NGO support. No traveler-facing documented restriction. Prevalence figures dated/LGBTQ-wide — no weight. Social hostility at political level (tier 3-ish) with recourse on paper but inconsistent. 0.62 seems right. Maybe 0.64.

Dossier 2: documented police practice targeting trans women — tier 2, state-tolerated; 38% arrest survey; 135 harassment cases; violence listed as significant human rights issue. But never criminalised, official welcoming posture, visible scene, pride since 2003. The police targeting is mainly sex workers, but the arrest stat is broad among trans women. For a visitor, exposure: police harassment/extortion of visibly trans people documented. That's tier 2. Severity moderate-high. Score ~0.46.

Final numbers: 1: 0.63, 2: 0.46, 3: 0.72, 4: 0.69, 5: 0.90.
